accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England Year 5 fractions statement 'add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, and denominators that are multiples of the same number', Year 6 'add and subtract fractions with different denominators and mixed numbers, using the concept of equivalent fractions', and CCSS 5.NF.A.1. Every sum recomputed: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4; 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12; 1/2 + 1/3 = 6/12 + 4/12 = 10/12 = 5/6 (2/5 = 4.8/12 < 6/12); 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12 with LCM(4, 6) = 12; 5/6 − 1/3 = 5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2; 3/4 + 1/2 = 5/4 = 1 1/4; 2/3 − 1/6 = 1/2. Sorter sums: 7/12, 5/6 and 3/4 are below 1; 5/4, 7/6 and 7/6 are above. Parameterised answers checked at their range corners by the items gate.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented fraction-addition errors (NCETM Year 5/6 fractions guidance; Ni and Zhou 2005 on whole-number bias; Siegler et al. 2013 on fraction arithmetic errors): adding numerators and denominators (2/6, 2/5, 2/9), scaling the denominator but not the numerator (1/4 + 1/4), adding the two denominators to make a 'common' one (10 for quarters and sixths), using a denominator the other does not go into (sixths for quarters), subtracting denominators (4/3), and not recognising an answer over one whole (5/4). The lab's Add button refuses unequal pieces, and the number line shows 2/5 lands left of 1/2.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab, including flag_fadd.js (same-denominator sums), flag_frac.js (equivalent fractions), flag_simpfrac.js and flag_fcmp.js. Only this lab lets the learner re-cut two different fraction bars until their piece sizes match, refuses to combine unequal pieces, hunts the lowest common denominator against two multiples lists, and subtracts by crossing out matched pieces.

lab_teaches.evidence: Six steps: cut halves into quarters and add; cut both thirds and quarters into twelfths; drag a dot on a twelfths line to place 1/2 + 1/3 (the halves segment is shown, the thirds segment appears after a miss); find twelfths, not twenty-fourths, for 1/4 + 1/6 (a correct 10/24 is accepted as true but sent back for the lowest); take 1/3 from 5/6 with crossed-out pieces; then the challenge. Each banner states the rule only after the learner has made the pieces match.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 1/2 + 1/4 (2/6 and 2/4 tempting), whether 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 ('1 + 1 = 2 and 2 + 3 = 5'), and 5/6 − 1/3 (4/3 from subtracting the bottoms, 4/6 from not rescaling). The reveal names the learner's own choice after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eight distinct wrong-answer messages: add the bottoms, change only the bottom, sum of denominators as common denominator, non-multiple denominator, shrinking the pieces when adding (5/8), subtracting denominators, 'a half and a third make a whole', and 'two fractions make more than one'. Each names the slip and gives the correct working.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text grade 1.8 and adult 6.1, well inside 6.5 and 9.5. Kid paragraphs use pizza-style pieces and short sentences; 'equivalent fractions' is defined where it first appears. Canvas banners wrap to at most three short lines at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler patterns and the explanation is under 12% shingle overlap with 521 (same-denominator sums), 13 (equivalent fractions) and 894 (simplifying fractions). Each kid paragraph does one job: why pieces must match, equivalent fractions, cutting both, and the add-the-bottoms trap plus subtraction.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 (2x) in light and dark, before and after Show me, for all six steps: both bars, labels and the result bar fit; the 4s/6s multiples rows fit on one line; the twelfths line keeps 0, 1/2 and 1 readable; footer messages wrap to two lines. Step 4 spacing was tightened after the first sheet showed the result line touching the footer.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap or drag has a button twin (Cut each bar, Add or Take away, move the dot back or on one twelfth, Check). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with both fractions, whether the pieces match, the dot position and the result. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors.
